lines.en: label yukicamp2:
scene yukiwater1
There’s some sort of riverbank or something along those lines that runs through the campsite.

And, after following it for several minutes out of sheer boredom or despondence or the inability to currently spend time with my niece, I wind up at a clearing made less clear by the inclusion of Yuki.
Which isn’t to say she’s an unwelcome contaminant despite the fact that her blood is the least drinkable of everyone’s here. Probably.
I don’t know much about cannibalism, but I do know that she’d be the last one among us I’d be willing to eat and it wouldn’t be due to the way I feel about her.
But how even do I feel about her?
I like her enough to not cannibalize her. That much is true.
But does that “like” extend beyond the reaches of Armin Meiwes and into a basket you could strap to a bicycle on a long ride through Rotenburg?

The implied proposal here is meant to isolate each trace of carnality and force you into an escapable (yet entirely metaphorical) line at your local department of motor vehicles or grocery store or something of the like.

Anywhere you could go reluctantly before finding yourself in a row full of other somewhat depressed and dejected people while thinking to yourself, “I’m in too deep now” or “If I leave, I’ll look awkward or weak.”
I think that not knowing how you feel about someone is a lot like finding yourself in one of those places. Or finding yourself hovering over the corpse of one who has agreed to be eaten.
I think I’d allow Yuki to eat me if she really wanted to.
She probably doesn’t, but I think I would let her. And I think I would let her because I think it’d be what I deserve.
But love and like are more than just bleeding out into a bathtub, right? Love and like and lovely and likely. But they’re also hateful in the fact that I’d hate to ever love or like love or like.
In the midst of this half-hearted delusion or doubt or whatever you want to call it, my mind takes a dip in the river — but my heart is in Rotenburg.
And so is every other piece of me.

If anyone is reading this or hearing this or watching this or whatever it is you’re supposed to be doing or think that you’re doing or are only doing because I think you’re supposed to hear or read or listen, know this.
I’m not very fond of bugs.
But I will never take pleasure in killing them.
: Yuki.
scene yukiwater2
: Hm?
: The fuck you doin’ over there? Just standin’ around and watching me like that makes you look like some kind of stalker.
: I didn’t know what else to do.
: Don’t wanna hang out with any of the others? Figured you were way closer to them than you are to me.
: Is that why you’re alone? You feel like you don’t fit in?
scene yukiwater3
: Nah. It ain’t anything that dramatic. Just trying to relax a little.
: I ain’t got a lot of experience with camping and shit, but I ain’t no stranger to sleepin’ outside. Shit like that was actually pretty normal back when I was younger.
: But hey, when you ain’t got a place to live, you make do with what you’ve got.
: And sometimes, all you’ve got is a bench in some town you can’t even remember the name of and a bunch of other girls drinking and laughing while you just want to sleep.
: Do you ever miss it? Being wild and free?
: Miss when my knees didn’t hurt. And when I wasn’t so fuckin’ tired all the time.
: And yeah, maybe I do miss the “freedom” part a little. But what I’ve got goin’ on now ain’t all that bad when you compare it to everything else I’ve lived through.
: Everything apart from how your upbringing wasn’t ever terrible to begin with, right?
scene yukiwater4
: You remember that, huh?
: My memory’s pretty terrible, but there are certain things that’ll always stick out to me.
: Things like girls who grew up in candy stores?
: Things like the minor details that have turned the people I like spending time with into people I like spending time with.
: Then tell me, what else do you remember about me?
: I remember how Yumi was made.
: Oh yeah? You the one who came inside me when I was passed out? Answer carefully or I’ll be on your case for over a decade’s worth of child support.
: That’s not what I was implying.
scene yukiwater5
: Then why the fuck did you word it like you were there watching the magic happen? You don’t know shit, man.
: I wish I had a better answer for you, but even the words inside of my head are sewn together strangely at times.
: Yeah, well you’re one of those creative types, ain’t ya? Complete opposite of people like me who never stuck around to learn about proverbs or pronouns.
: On the bright side, you could beat me in a fight. So if the world breaks out into a war-zone, you’ll probably outlast me.
: World’s already turned into a war-zone. But somehow, people like us have managed to avoid it.
: You’ve avoided it because you have a vagina. I’ve avoided it because I-
: Also have a vagina?
scene yukiwater6
: Sorry. Did I hurt your feelings?
: Yes. And I am ending our friendship as a result of this. Goodbye, Yuki.
: Damn, really? Oh well. Guess I’ll have to just empty out this entire cooler all by myself.
: Are you apologizing in the form of giving me free alcohol?
: Free? No way. I’m a bartender now. You tip me for this shit.
: Unfortunately, I left all of my cash at home on account of convenience stores not existing in the woods.
scene black
: I’ll just add it to your tab then. Been keepin’ a close eye on that shit since Sara’s always givin’ you booze for free.
: I have a tab?
: Damn right. And I’m the type of girl who always collects, if you know what I mean.
: It’s always impressive how you’re able to both strong-arm me and flirt at the same time.
scene yukiwater7
: Aight, first and foremost — I don’t strong-arm you into anything. And, if I do, it ain’t intentional. Probably just a result of me being a badass or some shit. But second, this ain’t flirting.
: How would you know? You’ve never been in a real relationship before.
: Have you? Because it seems to me like you’re just the town bimbo a lot of the time.
scene yukiwater8
: That’s not far off, but...
: I have.
: Oh? Then maybe you do know what you’re talkin’ about. But still, we’re two different weight classes. And I ain’t about to go punchin’ at someone so much weaker than me.
: That’s fair. And I was just kidding in the first place. You’ve been surprisingly kind to me for someone who could kick my ass at any moment.
: Thank you for admitting that.
: And thank you for not eating me.
scene yukiwater9
: For what?
: When you were outside of Kumon-mi, what was it like?
: What do you mean?
: Like...you’ve been in this city long enough to understand how it feels, right? How no one comes in and no one goes out.
: That ain’t entirely true. Had a whole ass group of European dudes come into the bar the other night and I had to kick ‘em out since I’m the only one of us who knew any English.
scene yukiwater10
: You know English?
: Just the basic shit. “Hello. How are you doing? Where is the restroom?” Shit like that.
: Why?
: Picked it up from an old friend. One of those creative types, like you.
: Someone in your gang?
scene yukiwater11
: Something like that. But yeah, wound up havin’ to kick ‘em out since Sana and Sara were too embarrassed to even try.
scene yukiwater12
: Why do you think it’d be any different outside of here, though? You ain’t thinkin’ of hoppin’ the wall, are you?
: Is that even possible?
: Not with that attitude it ain’t. Moment you doubt yourself is the moment you fall several hundred feet and turn into a fuckin’ Sensei puddle.
scene yukiwater13
: Fair enough.
: I’ve just been wondering a lot lately about what it would be like to sort of...start over. But I feel like, as long as I’m here, that’ll never be possible.
: There’s too much tying me to this place. Too many things I’d rather just forget at this point because they make just getting through each day way harder than it should ever be.
scene yukiwater14
: Mm.
: Well, sorry to burst your bubble, but that shit’ll follow you even if you do manage to make it out of here, man. Just changin’ scenery ain’t enough to “start over.” I know that better than anybody.

: Like yeah, a new town might be exciting for a little while. You might be able to distract yourself from all that shit you’d “rather forget.” But the second you start to remember, you’ll have to move again.
: So you’ll move and you’ll move and you’ll move, but you’ll never get any further away from the shit you’re trying to escape from. And, soon enough, all those places will start to blur together.
: That’s sort of where I’m at. How there’s no “one town” that sticks out to me from my past because, if there was, I’d still be there.
scene yukiwater15
: Nobody can escape the past, man. All you can do is confront it. And hey, maybe you get your ass beat. Maybe you don’t.
: But there’s a lot more honor in goin’ down with a fight than just lying down and letting life kick the shit out of you.
: That may be true. But what good does something vague like “honor” do in the first place?
: What good does being a bitch do?
: Nothing really.
: Exactly. Cause nothing matters at all when shit really comes down to it.
: It’s up to us to figure out what we value. And honor’s kinda fuckin’ bred into us since our ancestors were probably samurai or some shit.

: If that doesn’t mean anything to you, then fuck it. But to me, honor and respect are, like...all I’ve got. Especially now that I’ve got a kid who might look back at me like you’re lookin’ at your past some day.
: I don’t wanna be something she’s gotta run from, you know? And the best way of doin’ that is by not settin’ an example and running away myself.
: You...You did, though. You did run.
scene yukiwater16
: Yeah, and look how that worked out. Shit didn’t change until I stopped. So maybe it’ll be the same for you.
scene yukiwater17
: I hate talking to you. You’re always wiser than I expect and none of my counterpoints ever last more than a second.
: Well, maybe you’ll be as wise as me in another decade or so. And this ain’t me sayin’ I’ve been through more since I don’t really know what your deal is yet, but...
: It’s clear you’ve been through a lot. And it’s that kinda shit that makes people call us “wise” when we’re wastin’ away our morning getting drunk by the river.
scene yukiwater18
: Thank you, Yuki.
: Hm? For what? Givin’ you advice even though you never asked for it?
: Everything, really.
: I’m glad you never gave up because that means I get to spend time with you now.
scene yukiwater19
: Wha-
: Ain’t...you just flirting now? Didn’t you just give me shit a few minutes ago after accusin’ me of the same damn thing?
: I wasn’t giving you shit. I was just trying to mold another conversation into a shape that wouldn’t force me to accept something I’m already beginning to understand.
scene yukiwater20
: Well...I’ve got no fuckin’ clue what you mean by that, but...be careful about what you say and shit.
: Why?
: Because I said so, okay?
: Is just admitting that I enjoy spending time with you really enough to make you this bashful? Is that seriously your only weakness?
scene yukiwater21
: Okay. Listen up, douchebag. Ain’t nobody ever actually shown me that sorta kindness before. So sorry if I’m reacting weirdly to it after fuckin’ decades without any experience at all.
: Why are you apologizing? I like this side of you.
scene yukiwater22
: Jesus, fuck! Stop!
: I might be your senior, but I’m still a fuckin’ girl, you know? And between this and all that shit about callin’ me cute a while ago, you’re gonna fuckin’...confuse me or something.
: I wish everyone reacted to honesty this way. It would make my life a hell of a lot easier.
scene yukiwater23
: Yeah, well...all it does is make mine harder.
: How so?
: Yuki?
: I wonder how you would’ve felt about me if we met when we were younger. Like...teenagers or some shit.
: You’re almost ten years older than me, aren’t you? I can’t imagine you’d have had any interest in me back then.
: I meant more, like...it’d be cool if we were the same age back then. Just wanna know how you’d feel about the old me rather than the burnout you’re wastin’ your time on now.
: I doubt we would have meshed well, to be honest.
: Yeah, you’re probably right.
: We’re practically opposites even now, aren’t we?
: Yeah, but...is that really a bad thing?
: It ain’t bad, but...it ain’t really good either. Not sure if we’ll ever, like...see eye-to-eye on anything.
: That’ll just keep our talks interesting then.
: Well...I’m gonna-
: Listen...uh...Sensei...
: If you, like...
: If you’re actually...like...
: If you actually think I’m...you know...cute or whatever...
: Could you, like...not say that anymore?

: Sara’s my boss, but like...she’s also a friend and shit. And she’s crazy about you whether you like that or not, so...I ain’t about to go, like...makin’ that more complicated, if you know what I mean.
: This is all just...assumin’ you ain’t bullshittin’ me, though. Cause I ain’t really got any idea...
: Do you actually like me, Yuki?

: Fuck if I know, man. All I know is that this blows and I keep wishin’ the fuckin’ circumstances were different. Cause I feel like Yumi’d be pissed about this too and I ain’t about to ruin shit again with her.
: Yeah...
: I wouldn’t want to do that to you either.
scene black
: I’m gonna walk around for a little while. But I’ll see you around the campsite.
: Thanks for the beer. And also the advice.
: And also for existing.
: Just...get lost, man. You’re interrupting my alone time.
scene sky
I leave Yuki by the riverside with all the same decaying parts and pieces she had when I first showed up.
But, for a brief moment in time, I imagine how much better they’d have tasted if we could turn back the clocks.
They’re all without hands now.
They’re just like dinner.
